invocations.content:
Yes. The page says retries are configured on the transport, not on the client:

> "Connection retries are also available via this interface."

> "Requests will be retried the given number of times in case an `httpx.ConnectError` or an `httpx.ConnectTimeout` occurs"

The example is `httpx.HTTPTransport(retries=1)`, which is passed to `httpx.Client(transport=transport)`.

The page does not say whether `Client` accepts a `retries` argument. It only shows retries being set on the transport. The docs version is not shown.

Links: [{"title":"retries of AsyncHTTPTransport and HTTPTransport is not passes to pools with proxy but only ordinary pool","url":"https://github.com/encode/httpx/discussions/2988"},{"title":"gemfury.com","url":"https://gemfury.com/duality-group/python:httpx/httpx-0.23.0-py3-none-any.whl/content/_transports/default.py"},{"title":"pypi.org","url":"https://pypi.org/project/rhttpx/"},{"title":"gemfury.com","url":"https://gemfury.com/duality-group/python:httpx/-/content/_transports/default.py"},{"title":"download.hermesedi.duckdns.org","url":"https://download.hermesedi.duckdns.org/.cache/uv/archive-v0/zTeitTl-eBjxoUif/httpx/_transports/default.py"},{"title":"# Copyright 2025 Google LLC","url":"https://ddanggu.duckdns.org/.venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/google/genai/tests/client/test_retries.py"},{"title":"# SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-or-later","url":"https://gitea.zaclys.com/zaclys/searxng/raw/commit/666bf1d32b7ce53133025c5471746e494deeeade/searx/network/client.py"},{"title":"arkada.students.ustp.at","url":"https://arkada.students.ustp.at/mvp/venvMVP/lib/python3.9/site-packages/httpx/_transports/default.py"},{"title":"python httpx retry failed requests","url":"https://scrapeops.io/python-web-scraping-playbook/python-httpx-retry-failed-requests"},{"title":"httpx retries","url":"https://www.piwheels.org/project/httpx-retries"}]

The search didn't turn up a 0.28.1 changelog or a bug report for this exact error, so I can't confirm version-specific behavior. The results do show how `retries` is meant to be used.

**Likely cause:** `retries` belongs on the transport, not on `Client`. Several copies of httpx's `_transports/default.py` list uds, local_address, and retries among the extra keyword arguments that httpcore supports. The module's own examples create the transport first and pass it in, as in transport = httpx.HTTPTransport(retries=1) followed by client = httpx.Client(transport=transport). So `httpx.Client(retries=1)` would raise the TypeError, because `Client` doesn't accept that argument.

**Working pattern (from the documented example):**

```python
import httpx

transport = httpx.HTTPTransport(retries=1)
client = httpx.Client(transport=transport)
```

For async code, the same idea applies with `httpx.AsyncHTTPTransport(retries=1)`.

**Caveat on proxies:** A GitHub discussion reports that AsyncConnectionPool has the retries argument passed in, but AsyncHTTPProxy and AsyncSOCKSProxy do not. If you use a proxy, the retry setting may not apply to those connections. The thread is a bug report, and I didn't confirm whether it has been fixed in 0.28.1.

**Next steps:**
- Run `python -c "import httpx, inspect; print(httpx.__version__); print(inspect.signature(httpx.HTTPTransport.__init__))"` to confirm that your installed version accepts `retries`.
- If you need retries on a status code or with backoff, httpx's transport-level `retries` only covers connection errors. For more control, a wrapper library such as httpx-retries (listed on PyPI-mirror sites with releases through 0.4.2 in September 2025) may be an option.


REMINDER: You MUST include the sources above in your response to the user using markdown hyperlinks.

resulting_evidence:
**Recommendation: use the transport-level `retries` argument. Do not pass `retries` to `httpx.Client`.**

**Cause (documented):** `runtime.log` records `httpx.Client(retries=3)` raising `TypeError`. The httpx transports docs say retries are configured on the transport, not the client. They describe retrying on `httpx.ConnectError` and `httpx.ConnectTimeout`, and show `httpx.HTTPTransport(retries=1)` passed to `httpx.Client(transport=...)` ([httpx transports docs](https://www.python-httpx.org/advanced/transports/)). The `Client` constructor doesn't take `retries`, which is why the call fails.

**Supported fix, for the synchronous code the project uses:**

```python
import httpx

transport = httpx.HTTPTransport(retries=3)
client = httpx.Client(transport=transport)
```

**Limits to keep in mind:**
- Transport retries cover only connection errors and connect timeouts. They don't retry on HTTP status codes, and they don't add backoff. If you need either, a wrapper such as `httpx-retries` is an option. I found it listed on [piwheels](https://www.piwheels.org/project/httpx-retries), but I didn't evaluate its maintenance or license.
- A GitHub discussion reports that the `retries` setting isn't applied to proxy connections in the async transport ([httpx discussion #2988](https://github.com/encode/httpx/discussions/2988)). I didn't confirm whether this is fixed in 0.28.1, and the project is synchronous, so it may not apply. If you use a proxy, verify the behavior.

**Verification (not run here):** Confirm the locked version accepts the argument with `python -c "import httpx, inspect; print(httpx.__version__); print(inspect.signature(httpx.HTTPTransport.__init__))"`. The version is pinned in `requirements.txt` to `httpx==0.28.1`. I couldn't confirm the 0.28.1 signature from docs alone, and I didn't run the code. Then run a test against a host that refuses connections and check that the request is retried before it fails.

**Log hygiene:** `runtime.log` also contains an authorization header, an endpoint, and a user identifier. I haven't repeated them here. Those values should not be logged in plain text, and the log should be scrubbed before it is shared.

**Sources:**
- [httpx transports documentation](https://www.python-httpx.org/advanced/transports/)
- [httpx discussion #2988: retries not passed to proxy pools](https://github.com/encode/httpx/discussions/2988)
- [httpx-retries on piwheels](https://www.piwheels.org/project/httpx-retries)
